page.layout: One page of text, running head at top with page number 119 at right; main text in one column; a signature-like mark "H 4" and catchword "Candei" at the foot of the text; faint marginal text in the left margin (cropped, partly illegible, not transcribed).

main_text.p: hominum viscera sunt persecuti, eorumque sapores.
Æthiopum gens, cuius regio à Neroë ad fluuium Hydaspin porrigitur, scorpionibus vescebatur aspidibusque.

Quintinus Heduus scribit, se vidisse in insula Melita, qui scorpionem ederet innoxie. Sunt enim illic scorpiones veneni expertes. Supra Borysthenem esse gentem Sauromatum, quæ tertio semper die capiat cibum: Ad extremos vero Indiæ fines gentem Astomorum fuisse, sine ore, corpore toto hirtam, vestitam frondium lanugine, halitibus tantum viventem & odore, quem naribus trahebant, memoria proditum est: quæ si vera sunt, quis miretur Democritum mellis odore vixisse.
Qui Athon montem incolebant, viperinis carnibus alebantur, itaque nec capiti nec vestibus eorum noxia corpori animalia innascebantur.
Pandoræ locustas in cibis habuerunt atque etiam Parthi.
Gens Medunnorum appellata animalium, quæ Cynocephalos vocabant, lacte viuebant. Arimphæi gens baccis alebatur.
Celenophagi testudinibus vescebantur, quarum testis casas suas integebant, idque genus hominum noua India alit:

page.notes: Left margin contains faint, cropped marginal notes that are not legible enough to transcribe. The word "Candei" at the foot is a catchword; the line "H 4" is the gathering signature. The line "Candei" also appears at the right of the last line of text and is noted as catchword.
